`notes-lib` is an in-memory notes library (`NoteStore`, `searchNotes`) that can only be used in-process. Other

so the deployment can be checked from end to end.

`NoteStore.add` and `searchNotes`. The HTTP layer only turns their `Result` into a status code. No business rules are
duplicated.

- 5 endpoints work as specified: `POST /notes`, `GET /notes`, `GET /notes/:id`, `GET /search?q=`, `GET /health`.
- 100% of the 5 existing tests still pass, and the new HTTP tests pass under `npm test`.
- 0 ESLint errors with complexity limit 8 (and the existing 40-line function limit), and 0 `tsc --noEmit` errors.
- 0 new runtime dependencies in `package.json` (only `node:` built-ins are used at runtime).

- `docker compose up` serves the API on host port 8081, and `curl -fsS http://localhost:8081/health` succeeds within
  120 s.
- `npm run smoke` exits 0 against a healthy deployment and exits non-zero when any of its 4 checks fails.

## Out of scope
- Persistence: notes stay in memory and are lost on restart.
- Authentication, update/delete endpoints, pagination.

{"stdout":"# Notes HTTP API (brownfield feature)

Add an HTTP API in front of the existing notes library.

## Requirements
- `POST /notes` with JSON {title, body} creates a note (201 + the note incl. id); an empty title returns 400.
- `GET /notes` lists notes; `GET /notes/:id` returns one note or 404.
- `GET /search?q=term` returns matching notes using the existing search function; an empty `q` returns 400.
- `GET /health` returns 200 {"status":"ok"}.
- Reuse the existing NoteStore and searchNotes. Follow the repository's existing conventions (see its README and tooling): library functions never throw and return Result<T>; HTTP status mapping happens only at the edge. No new runtime dependencies (use node:http).
- Deployment: `Dockerfile` (node:24-alpine) and `docker-compose.yml` exposing the service on host port 8081; `scripts/smoke.ts` run by `npm run smoke` exercises /health, creating a note, fetching it and searching it against http://localhost:8081, exiting non-zero on any failure.

## Non-functional requirements
- Every endpoint responds in under 50 ms (p95) locally for up to 1,000 stored notes.
- The 5 existing tests keep passing and the lint complexity limit (8) and type check stay clean.
- The service logs one line per request and never logs request bodies.
